# Reference-angle diagnostic findings — 2018-11-01 and 2018-11-05

**Source:** Four plotted overlap groups in `figures/reference_audit_group_{01,02,04,05}.png`; numerical results in [reference_angle_diagnostics.csv](reference_angle_diagnostics.csv). These were generated by `validate_reference_methods.py` using identical one-second FIELDS measurements and the two different reference directions.

## Quantitative observations

| Group | UTC | 1-s paired samples | Median absolute angle difference | Local above 45° | Parker-SPC above 45° |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | Nov 1, 18:20–19:17 | 3781 | 16.93° | 79.82% | 80.56% |
| 2 | Nov 5, 13:34–13:41 | 771 | 15.25° | 13.23% | 25.42% |
| 4 | Nov 5, 13:44–13:58 | 1211 | 7.60° | 42.20% | 45.58% |
| 5 | Nov 5, 13:59–14:10 | 1009 | 4.23° | 47.37% | 44.50% |

Percentages above 45° are **fractions of commonly valid one-second samples within each diagnostic plot window, including plotting padding**. They are not event occurrence rates, confidence scores, or physical switchback probabilities.

## Visual inspection of the four graphs

- **Group 1 (Nov 1):** The local deflection briefly drops beneath the 30° boundary near 18:47 UTC, separating two intervals. The Parker-SPC deflection stays higher through the gap and links them. The scalar field magnitude exhibits pronounced changes, so physical classification remains uncertain.
- **Group 2 (Nov 5):** Parker-SPC angles are systematically higher over much of the plotted segment; some earlier deflections exceed 30° or 45° under SPC but not under the local reference. A change in magnetic components and magnitude near 13:39 UTC further complicates assigning a single event boundary. This group has the largest difference in 45° exceedance fraction.
- **Group 4 (Nov 5):** The two angle curves track relatively closely but encounter a low-angle gap near 13:49 UTC. The SPC reference splits this activity into two threshold-defined events, while the local reference treats it as one longer event. Differences in threshold residence time and the 20-second merging condition are plausible contributors.
- **Group 5 (Nov 5):** Both deflection curves almost coincide (4.23° median absolute difference). The SPC catalog contains an additional short interval near 14:09–14:10 UTC. The discrepancy is therefore boundary/segmentation-sensitive rather than evidence for an entirely separate physical phenomenon.

The above are qualitative interpretations of the figures, **not independently established switchback labels or a measured causal decomposition** of the angle-reference differences.

## Decisions supported, and not supported

**Supported:** The background reference changes the absolute deflection angle, threshold-crossing times, and number or extent of detected intervals. Temporal-overlap grouping reveals these as segmentation disagreements, rather than fully disjoint activity.

**Not yet supported:** The local or Parker-SPC detector being more physically accurate; sensitivity, specificity, false-positive rate; completed replication of Laker et al. 2022; population-wide occurrence rates.

The [manual review sheet](reference_review_sheet.csv) currently contains blank classification fields. Those fields should stay empty until review criteria and independent evidence justify a label.

The optional plot `figures/reference_audit_laker2019_example.png` was **not present in GitHub when this audit was written**, so the published August 31, 2019 check cannot yet be counted as performed. The independently selected E1–E2 switchback catalog from [Martinović et al.](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4579821) is a promising source of external positive examples, but uses joint magnetic/plasma visual selection and has not yet been cross-matched.

## Next objective

Cross-match detector candidates against independently selected positives **on the same observation times**; separately choose representative reviewed non-events and assess boundary quality and data quality. A published *positive-only* catalog cannot on its own measure specificity or an unbiased false-positive rate.
